title: Trains to Cosford
from: the main stations around the country
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the RAF Cosford Air Show. Cosford has its own little station right by the airfield, and West Midlands Railway stops there once an hour each way on its Birmingham to Shrewsbury trains. That one hourly train is the bit to plan around. I’ve added connections from the big stations that work well too, like Avanti from London Euston, CrossCountry from Leeds and Nottingham, and Transport for Wales from Cardiff and Manchester. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the RAF Cosford Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: Cosford station sits right next to the airfield, so it’s only about 300 metres to the show. On show day there are staff and signs, and honestly you can just follow everyone else. There is no step free access to the platforms, so if you use a wheelchair or struggle with steps, please take a look at the show’s accessibility page before you book.
walkBack: Allow about 10 minutes to walk back to the station, and a lot longer when the flying finishes, as there’s a queue system at the station when it gets busy.
tip: Only one train an hour stops at Cosford each way on a normal Sunday, so I would plan the Cosford train first and work back from it. Missing it by a minute can mean nearly an hour on the platform.
The station gets very busy straight after the flying. I would either leave during a display you’re less bothered about, or stay and look round the stalls, get some food and let the first rush go.

In past years West Midlands Railway has run extra trains after the show, and some Transport for Wales trains that don’t normally stop have called at Cosford. The summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.
alt: When I last checked, an off peak day return from Wolverhampton was £6.20 and from Birmingham New Street £11.00, so the short hops are cheap.

From further away, booking an advance ticket on the long leg can save a lot. If you’re going as a family, a Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, so it may well pay for itself on this one trip.
note: Times are from the National Rail timetable for Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026, so they are a guide to how Sunday trains run rather than the show day times. The big stations and city termini further from Cosford use the times for Sunday 15 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. Sunday times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, and extra trains are often added for the show, so please check before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: West Midlands Railway, plus the connections that work well. Every journey ends on the West Midlands Railway train that stops at Cosford. I’ve only included connections from the big stations where the change is sensible and the whole trip works on a Sunday. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there. I’ve also added eight c2c stations, with the c2c train into London and the connection on from there.

about.Wolverhampton|Shrewsbury: Through the Shropshire countryside, past Cosford and the airfield, then Telford and Wellington with the Wrekin in view.
about.Cosford|Telford Central: A short run through Shifnal and on into Telford.

pay: From further away, an Advance ticket on the long leg can save a lot, but it ties you to one train. I would plan the hourly Cosford train first, then book the train that connects with it.
When I last checked, an off peak day return from Wolverhampton was £6.20 and from Birmingham New Street £11.00, so there’s no need to book those ahead.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, so it may well pay for itself on this one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Cosford. It has its own little station right next to the airfield, about 300 metres from the show.
How often do trains stop at Cosford?
On a normal Sunday only one train an hour stops each way, so I would plan around that train and work back from it. In past years extra trains have run after the show.
There’s no step free access to the platforms at Cosford. If you use a wheelchair or struggle with steps, please take a look at the show’s accessibility page before you book.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
I’m coming from further away. What do I do?
I would plan your trip to one of the twelve stations here first, then pick up the connection to Cosford from there.
access: Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
Cosford has no step free access to its platforms, so I would book Passenger Assist and check which side your train home leaves from.
